reason: E1 directly supports precipitate formation, dislocation/grain-boundary pinning, and improved high-temperature strength with unchanged room-temperature performance at 0.5 at.% Hf, but provides no evidence regarding density, which is a key premise of the hypothesis.
premises: Trace Hf (~0.5 at.%) forms fine Hf-rich precipitates at interfaces and within certain phases in refractory HEAs.
These precipitates impede dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding at high temperature.
This precipitation strengthening improves high-temperature strength without substantially altering room-temperature ductility.
The Hf addition does not significantly change the alloy's density.
The effect is specific to trace amounts; higher Hf content may be detrimental.
